why: The finiteness of $I$ and $J$ is asserted HERE as well, inside the lemma, and Lean asserts it once — `variable {I J : Type*} [Fintype I] [Fintype J]`. So the `variable` line is in this region and in `thm`, shared exactly as in `item1/root` (same paper, same double statement).

'has maximum rank among all real matrices supported on $T$' is the hypothesis `hmax`, but the paper never defines `rank` and writes it for the first and only time in the proof's last line — a forward reference, same as in `item1`.
'supported on $T$' twice in one lemma, defined in the paragraph above.
The conclusion this negates — without it 'instead' names nothing. Same back-reference as `item1/root/1.1`.
Where the reductio opened here is discharged, nine sentences later.
'is still supported on $T$' needs the definition from thirteen lines earlier.
What $D$ is — the maximum-rank matrix fixed by the lemma's hypothesis.
Where $s$ and $j$ come from. $e_s$, $e_j^{\mathsf T}$ are never defined anywhere in the paper — the nearest it comes is this binder.
What $D_\tau$ is, from the previous sentence; $D_\tau x=\tau x_j e_s$ is a computation from that definition.
That $x\in\ker D$ is what makes the $D$ term of $D_\tau x$ vanish; the paper never shows the cancellation.
The equation this concludes from, immediately above.
The step needs $x_j\ne0$ to divide by $\tau x_j$ — from the reductio supposition, not from anywhere near this sentence.
What $D_\tau$ is; $Dw=D_\tau w-\tau w_j e_s$ is that rearranged.
Why the right-hand side lies in $\im D_\tau$: by definition and by the previous sentence.
The 'so' makes this a conclusion of the previous sentence, which is where all the content is.
That $y\in\ker D^{\mathsf T}$ is why '$y$ annihilates $\im D$' is true — eleven lines up.
$y_s\ne0$ is asserted flatly here, but it follows from the reductio supposition, not from anything nearby.
One half of 'Therefore': $\im D\subseteq\im D_\tau$.
The other half: strictness of the inclusion.
The maximality that is contradicted, fifteen lines up.
Why `hmax` applies to $D_\tau$ at all — step 1.2.
